transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-09-17
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Samantha Ruiz (HelixWave), Ethan Cole (HelixWave), Rhea Kapoor (HelixWave)

Summary:
High-level console walkthrough focused on per-route usage analytics, cost decomposition, and options for pilot (hosted vs dedicated). Customer concerned about unit economics, data residency and KMS.

Topics:
- Console: usage paths and per-route dashboards
- Cost breakdown: per-route, per-token, embedding vs generation
- Routing policies: latency vs cost
- Security: SOC2, KMS, VPC/private
- Pilot scope and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick off, um, quick intro — I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood, and with me is Liam, our solutions engineer.
[00:07] Samantha Ruiz: Hi, Samantha here — Head of Platform at HelixWave. Thanks for squeezing us in, we wanted to focus on how you break down costs per feature path, like Chat -> Summarize -> Search endpoints.
[00:15] Liam Ortiz: Yep, great. We'll jump into the console, show per-route lenses, the cost decomposition, and then the Optimize suggestions for batching and quantization.
[00:24] Ethan Cole: Quick note — FinOps needs to see expected monthly burn for 5 million tokens, and we need to map those to our product teams.
[00:32] Jordan Park: Understood. Rhea, are you owning the sample traffic export? That will help the cost modeling.
[00:37] Rhea Kapoor: I can pull weekly logs, yeah. We use a mix of embeddings for search and text generation for summaries, roughly 70/30.
[00:45] Liam Ortiz: Cool. Ok, sharing my screen — this is the Routes dashboard, you'll see top-left the global usage heatmap, then per-route tiles. Each tile breaks down tokens, latency P95, and cost per 1k tokens.
[01:02] [screen noise] Liam Ortiz: One thing, the transcription might say 'KA cache' sometimes — it's KV cache, sorry.
[01:10] Samantha Ruiz: That's fine. Walk us through how you attribute cost to routes — is it based on route tags or service name?
[01:18] Liam Ortiz: We allow both. You can tag incoming requests at the SDK level or via header routing, and the console aggregates by tag. For attribution we use the route ID plus model variant — so if you run a cheaper quantized variant behind the same route, it shows as a separate cost line.
[01:35] Ethan Cole: So we can see 'Search-prod-embed' vs 'Search-prod-llm' separately?
[01:39] Liam Ortiz: Exactly. And the cost breakdown shows raw GPU time estimate, token billing estimate, and an infra amortization line — that's our reserved capacity allocation when you're on Dedicated.
[01:51] Samantha Ruiz: How accurate are those infra amort numbers? We have reserved instances elsewhere and need predictable mapping.
[01:58] Jordan Park: The console uses your committed capacity profile and training/compute hours to apportion fixed infra costs across routes. For hosted customers it's an estimate, for Dedicated customers we can pull actual usage from your reserved pool which makes it within ~5% accuracy.
[02:13] Rhea Kapoor: How do you handle cache hit savings — say we have prefix caching for summarization, will the console show token savings?
[02:20] Liam Ortiz: Yes, we show cache hit rate and the estimated 'avoided tokens' metric — it's a separate column in the per-route table. Also our Optimize engine will recommend prefix caching policies for high-duplicate prompts.
[02:33] Ethan Cole: On the Optimize suggestions — does it automatically recommend quantization levels? We're sensitive about output quality.
[02:39] Liam Ortiz: It suggests quantization profiles per-model and per-route based on your eval set and latency/cost targets. You can preview recommended profiles and run a quality check A/B — the console ties diffed eval results back to the route.
[02:52] Samantha Ruiz: If we accept a recommendation, is there a rollback? We need safety nets for production.
[02:57] Jordan Park: Yes — rollouts are canary-based, you can split traffic percentages, and automatic fallback to previous model variant if quality drops or latency SLO violated.
[03:08] [crosstalk] Rhea Kapoor: So for pilot we could start with 10% traffic to a quantized model and watch evals?
[03:12] Liam Ortiz: That's the standard approach. Also we have per-route SLO alerts — you'll get an alert if latency or quality regresses.
[03:20] Ethan Cole: Data residency — we need logs and KV cache to remain in our VPC. Is that possible in Private deployment?
[03:28] Jordan Park: Absolutely. Private gives you customer-managed VPC and optional on-prem. Our control plane remains separate unless you opt for the full Private control plane where nothing leaves your network.
[03:40] Samantha Ruiz: KMS integration — we use AWS KMS and an HSM for certain keys. How do you handle key management?
[03:47] Liam Ortiz: We support KMS and bring-your-own-HSM in Private. For hosted customers we integrate with customer-managed keys via cross-account access, and we log key usage. We'll send the KMS integration notes after the call.
[03:58] [00:03:59] Jordan Park: Competitors question — anyone comparing to Anthropic or hosted endpoints?
[04:05] Ethan Cole: We looked at Anthropic and Vertex but they don't have the same per-route economics tooling, that was our main pain.
[04:12] Liam Ortiz: Right. Another difference is our runtime-level batching and KV cache metrics which directly tie to cost savings you can measure in the console.
[04:22] Samantha Ruiz: How do you charge for embeddings vs generation? We run embeddings at scale.
[04:27] Jordan Park: Embeddings are shown as separate routes and token units are normalized; pricing tiers can be set per-route. For the POC we can set a separate quota and alerts so finance can see embeddings burn isolated.
[04:39] Rhea Kapoor: Can we get a sample pricing sheet mapped to our projected 5M tokens? Like a line-item for each major route?
[04:45] Jordan Park: Yes — Jordan will send a per-route cost matrix. We'll plug your sample traffic and run a model selection + routing policy to give a monthly estimate and a sensitivity analysis.
[04:58] Ethan Cole: About SLA — what's included for Dedicated?
[05:03] Liam Ortiz: Dedicated includes an SLA for queueing latency and uptime, with credits for missed SLOs. We also have optional premium support blocks.
[05:11] Samantha Ruiz: Any gotchas — cold start, kv cache warmup?
[05:15] Liam Ortiz: Cache warmup can cause early higher latency; our recommendations include pre-warming sequences and a small warm traffic guard. Also cold-start variance is minimized by our preallocated pools in Dedicated.
[05:26] [05:26] Rhea Kapoor: Are there recommended practices for route naming? We have messy service names.
[05:31] Liam Ortiz: Route naming matters for attribution. We recommend a canonical naming scheme product-env-feature, e.g., search-prod-embed. The console supports mappings if you need to alias tags.
[05:42] Samantha Ruiz: Ok, recap — we want a) pricing mapped to our 5M tokens, b) SOC2 + security docs, c) a 3-week pilot scope, d) sample traffic analysis. Anything else?
[05:53] Jordan Park: We'll also include recommended quantization profiles and a proposed canary rollout plan for the pilot.
[06:00] Ethan Cole: Timelines — can we start pilot early October? We need purchase approval by end of September.
[06:07] Jordan Park: We can aim for 2025-10-01 pilot kickoff pending approvals. I'll follow up with pricing and a proposed pilot runbook.
[06:15] Samantha Ruiz: Great. Thanks, everyone.
[06:17] Jordan Park: Thanks — we'll close here. Liam and I will send the docs.

[12:00] Liam Ortiz: Jumping back in — now on the Cost Explorer. This view lets you slice by day, by route tag, by model family. You can also export hourly cost CSV to S3 for downstream FinOps tools.
[12:20] Ethan Cole: Export to S3 is important. We want hourly granularity and mapping to our internal cost center. Can you add a custom label?
[12:27] Liam Ortiz: Yep, you can define custom cost center tags and the export includes them.
[14:40] Rhea Kapoor: On instrumentation — do you capture user_id or PII in logs? We want to ensure we can mask or tokenize.
[14:47] Jordan Park: Logs can be configured to drop or hash PII at ingestion. For Private deployments we can also enable on-prem log sinks so nothing leaves the VPC.
[18:00] Liam Ortiz: Quick demo of SDK header tagging: here's a 2-line snippet, set header 'x-rd-route: search-prod-embed' — that flows through and shows up in the console attribution.
[20:10] Samantha Ruiz: Nice. For the sample traffic Rhea will upload, what's the expected format?
[20:17] Liam Ortiz: JSONL of requests with route header and timestamps works best. We'll provide a template.
[24:00] Jordan Park: Walkthrough of the Optimize tab — you'll see suggestions ranked by potential monthly savings. Each suggestion has estimated impact and a risk score.
[27:30] Ethan Cole: How do you calculate risk score?
[27:33] Liam Ortiz: It's heuristic: eval-quality delta, historical variance, and a model-specific quality baseline. You can tune sensitivity in the Optimize settings.
[30:00] Liam Ortiz: Autoscaling and burst — Dedicated supports guaranteed baseline and burst buckets. Burst draws from a shared pool, we meter burst separately so you can see actual burst spend in the console.
[33:20] Rhea Kapoor: Is there a hard cap to prevent runaway spend during a traffic spike?
[33:25] Jordan Park: Yes — per-route quotas and global caps exist. You can configure hard stop thresholds and soft alerts.
[36:40] Liam Ortiz: Observability — we emit per-request traces you can hook into Jaeger or our tracing UI. We also expose a per-route cost/time breakdown in traces to help perf debugging.
[38:10] Samantha Ruiz: For audit — how long do you retain audit logs? We need 12 months for compliance.
[38:17] Liam Ortiz: By default hosted retains 90 days; Dedicated and Private can extend retention to 12+ months with add-on retention blocks.
[41:00] Ethan Cole: Procurement questions — PO process and invoicing cadence?
[41:07] Jordan Park: We invoice monthly for hosted usage. For Dedicated we can do monthly or quarterly invoices against committed spend, and we accept PO/Net30 for enterprise contracts.
[44:12] Samantha Ruiz: Legal — any standard terms that are blockers for us? Data processing agreements?
[44:19] Jordan Park: We have a DPA and standard enterprise addenda; we'll share the legal pack. For Private deployments we can customize language around data residency.
[47:50] Liam Ortiz: Returning to the console — here's an anomaly detection alert feed. You can tune sensitivity and route-level channels (pager, slack, email).
[50:00] Rhea Kapoor: For the POC can we get a sandbox with synthetic traffic so we can validate rollouts without touching prod?
[50:07] Liam Ortiz: Yes, sandbox workspaces are standard. We'll provision a sandbox workspace and seed it with mock traffic so you can test A/B and canary safely.
[52:10] Ethan Cole: Okay finance will need a line-item estimate and a total cost of ownership doc; that plus the security pack will get us through approval.
[52:20] Jordan Park: We'll include a TCO slide that shows three scenarios: hosted, dedicated, private — with sensitivity to token volume and cache hit improvements.
[55:30] Samantha Ruiz: Any final questions from your side?
[55:34] Rhea Kapoor: One small one — is there a programmatic way to pull the per-route cost via API for our internal dashboards?
[55:40] Liam Ortiz: Yes, we have a Usage API that returns per-route breakdowns hourly. We'll send API keys for the trial environment.
[55:50] Jordan Park: Great — recap of next steps: pricing matrix, SOC2/security docs, KMS notes, sample traffic template, sandbox workspace, and proposed pilot runbook.
[56:05] Ethan Cole: Sounds good. We'll confirm internal go/no-go by Friday 2025-09-19.
[56:12] Jordan Park: Perfect. Thanks again.
[56:18] Samantha Ruiz: Thanks team.
[56:22] Jordan Park: End call.
